newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV FALTERS AHEAD OF FRENCH TITLE DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV FALTERS AHEAD OF FRENCH TITLE DEFENCE.

text.p: World number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov suffered a heavy blow ahead of his French Open title defence when he was knocked out of the Italian Open by Spain's Alberto Berasategui on Thursday.

Kafelnikov lasted less than hour against his unseeded opponent, losing 6-3 6-2 and then said it "would take a miracle" to retain the French crown at Roland Garros. The grand slam tournament starts on Monday week.

The Russian is desperately short of match practice after a three-month lay-off with a broken finger in his right hand, and his error-strewn performance against Berasategui earned him a chorus of boos from the Foro Italico faithful.
Kafelnikov's exit means just three seeded players have survived to the quarter-finals -- seventh seed Marcelo Rios of Chile, Spain's Alex Corretja, seeded 10, and sixth seed Goran Ivanisevic.
Ivanisevic saved four set-points before defeating German Boris Becker.
The lanky Croat, recovered from 3-6 down in a first set tiebreak to win 7-6 (9-7) 6-3 -- and then thanked God for his broken finger and a 20-day break from tennis prior to this tournament.
Ivanisevic is playing his first tournament since slamming his finger in a door and breaking it in three places in Barcelona last month.
"I was burnt out, a little bit sick of tennis, then luckily I got injured in a stupid way that only I can do," he said.

The world's top two Pete Sampras and Michael Chang, both American, were eliminated in the first round, and Austria's Thomas Muster and Dutchman Richard Krajicek -- last year's finalists -- were knocked out on Wednesday.
Ivanisevic will next meet Australian Scott Draper who brought Italian Davide Scala's brave run from the qualifiers to a halt.
Rios continued the rich vein of form that brought him the Monte Carlo title last month, defeating Swede Magnus Larsson in three sets to set up a quarter-final with American Jim Courier.
The unseeded Courier, champion here in 1992 and 1993 and conqueror of Sampras in the first round, made short work of 15th seed Marc Rosset of Switzerland.
Another seed, number 11 Albert Costa of Spain, also went out to Marc-Kevin Goellner of Germany 6-4 3-6 6-4, who must now meet Kafelnikov's conqueror Berasategui.
